title: skills/objectstack-automation: the inbound hook section does not say that a disabled package's flow answers 401 at the hook door (after #33906)
body:
domain:server#5 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jUZKdq3PK2Sab53cT3

Skills-docs follow-up owed by PR #34278 (#33906), declared there as `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md:383-395`. Filed by area S6.

**What changes once #34278 lands.** The anonymous inbound hook (`POST /api/v1/automation/hooks/...`) refuses a post whose resolved slot belongs to a registry-held package that is disabled, with the door's existing one `401 INVALID_SIGNATURE` (cause in the server log only), nothing enqueued, on both the bare address (a name one package holds) and the qualified `/:namespace/:flowName/:hookId` address. Re-enabling the package answers `202` again with no re-arm.

**The gap.** `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md` ~L383-395 (the hook endpoint table and bullets) says the endpoint ACKs `202` and enqueues, and names the `401` only for a flow name two packages hold. An agent following the skill would read a `401` from a disabled package's hook as a signature fault.

**Ask.** Add one bullet beside the two-holder bullet: a flow whose package is disabled answers the same `401 INVALID_SIGNATURE` (cause logged, never sent) until the package is enabled; senders that retry on a non-2xx keep the event and can redeliver after a re-enable. Run the skills gates (`check-skill-*`).

Dedupe words: skills automation inbound hook disabled package 401; SKILL.md hook disabled holder.
